claim: An employer's facially neutral shift-rotation policy was found to constitute unlawful disparate impact discrimination where statistical evidence demonstrated it disproportionately excluded Black employees from supervisory advancement tracks. The Fifth Circuit held that operational convenience cannot justify a practice whose discriminatory effect the employer failed to rebut with evidence of business necessity.
citation: Delacroix v. Meridian Freight Solutions, Inc., 738 F.2d 511 (5th Cir. 1984)
